mappings.name: transactionstatus: no record of this order

file: the only thing that moves money (docs/flows/reconciler.md).
Selection is by the body's `order_id`; `amount` and `pay_token`
travel in the same body and are deliberately NOT matched on, so a
suite that seeds any pay_token into ChargeRef::ref_extra works
Priority 1 for the per-reference cases, 10 for the catch-all SUCCESS
— which exists so `just up` plus a developer's curl behaves as it did
before this file was split out of webpayment.json.
Commentary lives in `metadata` because WireMock fails to start on a
mapping document containing any field it does not recognise.
comment: REF_UNKNOWN. 'I have no record' — must become
ChargeStatus::NotFound, never a failure: a charge the rail has not
heard of may still be one the payer is about to complete.
REF_UNAVAILABLE. A rail that is down must never look like a payer who
was declined: the adapter owes ProviderError::Transport
(Category::Rail), so the worker retries instead of the merchant
starting a new intent.

mappings.name: transactionstatus: answers after the request deadline

comment: REF_SLOW. 2000 ms against the suite's SHORT_REQUEST_TIMEOUT of
100 ms — two orders of magnitude, so the assertion is about the
deadline firing and not about a slow CI machine. The eventual body is
a success precisely so the test cannot pass for the wrong reason: if
the deadline did not fire, the adapter would answer Succeeded and the
'must be Transport' assertion would fail loudly.
The decline table's one Orange row: EXPIRED -> payer_timeout
(docs/flows/adapter-orange-money.md). The payer never entered the
one-time code before the hosted page aged out.

mappings.name: transactionstatus: failed with no documented sub-reason

comment: FAILED, for which Orange documents no sub-reason vocabulary, so the
adapter maps it to provider_error and carries `message` through as
the raw reason. Not in the conformance decline table — that table
holds only *documented* mappings; design §4 asks for the body to
exist.

jsonBody.message: Transaction refused by the payer's bank

comment: INITIATED: the token exists and the payer has not started. It is the
row a careless transcription turns into a failure, so it gets a stub
of its own even though no conformance case names it yet.

mappings.name: transactionstatus: scenario, pending on the first ask

comment: REF_SCENARIO, first call. A WireMock scenario rather than two
references, because the property under test is that query_status
reports what the rail says *now* and never caches its first answer —
the poll ladder in docs/flows/reconciler.md is built entirely on
that. This is the one stateful case, which is why every other case
uses a distinct reference and needs no admin reset between tests.
REF_SCENARIO, second call and thereafter: the payer entered the
one-time code.
The catch-all, at the lowest priority: anything not named above is a
settled payment. This is what compose.yml's stub answered before the
file was split, so `just up` behaves unchanged for a developer. It
cannot mask a broken per-reference match: every case above asserts
something other than 'succeeded', so a mapping that stopped matching
would fall through to here and fail its test.

mappings.name: transactionstatus: a body far larger than any answer this rail documents

comment: REF_HUGE. 300 KB, past vpay_provider::http::MAX_RAIL_BODY_BYTES (256 KiB).
Response::bytes() reads to end of stream, so the peer chose how much memory a worker
task allocated until the Step 3 security review; bounded_body stops at the cap.
A valid SUCCESS body on purpose: without the bound the adapter would parse it and
answer Succeeded, so the case cannot pass for the wrong reason. Padded via
--global-response-templating rather than a 300 KB fixture file.
